title: Write a Docker Compose File
intro: docker-tutorial-002 had you running an existing Compose stack. Now write one: a web app plus a Postgres database with persistent storage.

steps.prompt: Define two services. 'web': built from the current directory (build: .), port "8080:3000" (quoted!), depends_on db (as a list), and environment variable DATABASE_URL: postgres://db:5432/app (map form). 'db': image postgres:16, with a named volume 'db-data' mounted at /var/lib/postgresql/data. Declare 'db-data' under a top-level volumes key.
steps.hint: Top-level keys: services and volumes. Quote port mappings as a habit: YAML 1.1 parses some unquoted 'a:b' values as base-60 NUMBERS — an SSH mapping like 22:22 silently becomes the integer 1342. 8080:3000 happens to survive, but quoting every mapping avoids the whole class of bug. A named volume just needs 'db-data:' (empty value) under the top-level volumes key.
steps.solution:
services:
  web:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8080:3000"
    depends_on:
      - db
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://db:5432/app
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    volumes:
      - db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
volumes:
  db-data:
steps.fake_output:
[+] Running 3/3
 ✔ Network app_default   Created
 ✔ Container app-db-1    Started
 ✔ Container app-web-1   Started
steps.explanation: The app reaches the database at hostname 'db' (the service name) on Compose's automatic network, and the database's data survives 'docker compose down'.
steps.why: Using the service name 'db' in DATABASE_URL works because Compose gives every service a DNS name on a shared network — no IPs to hardcode (compare docker-incident-002, where plain docker run left containers on different networks). Note depends_on only controls START ORDER, not readiness: postgres may still be initializing when web starts, so the app should retry its connection (or use depends_on with condition: service_healthy plus a healthcheck).
